questions.questionText: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because iron oxide, or rust, covers much of its surface.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the galaxy in which our Solar System is located?
questions.explanation: Our Solar System is part of the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.questionText: Which is the largest planet in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in our Solar System by both diameter and mass.

questions.questionText: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is indeed a Star.

questions.questionText: Which planet is famous for its prominent rings?
questions.explanation: The rings of Saturn are made mostly of ice and rocky material.

questions.questionText: How many planets are in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Our Solar System has eight recognized planets. Pluto is considered as a Dwarf Planet

questions.questionText: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the innermost planet in our Solar System.

questions.questionText: What is Earth's natural satellite called?
questions.explanation: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite. (also called Luna)

questions.questionText: Which planet is known for rotating on its side?
questions.explanation: Uranus has an extreme axial tilt, so it rotates almost on its side.

questions.questionText: What force keeps planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun's gravity keeps the planets in their orbits.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the first artificial satellite launched into space?
questions.explanation: Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union in 1957.

questions.questionText: Which planet has the Great Red Spot, a giant storm?
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is a huge, long-lasting storm in Jupiter's atmosphere.

questions.questionText: What is a light-year a measure of?
questions.explanation: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.

questions.questionText: Which was the first human to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space in 1961.

questions.questionText: What process allows a star like the Sun to release energy?
questions.explanation: In the Sun's core, nuclear fusion combines hydrogen nuclei to form helium and releases energy.

questions.questionText: Which planet is the hottest on average in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Venus is hottest on average because its dense atmosphere traps heat through an intense greenhouse effect.

questions.questionText: What is the boundary around a black hole beyond which light cannot escape called?
questions.explanation: The Event Horizon is the boundary beyond which nothing, including light, can escape a black hole.

questions.questionText: Which space telescope launched in 2021 observes the universe mainly in infrared light?
questions.explanation: The James Webb Space Telescope launched in 2021 and is designed primarily for infrared observations.

questions.questionText: What causes the phases of the Moon?
questions.explanation: As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different portions of the Moon's sunlit half.

options.text: Earth's shadow always covering part of it
Different portions of its sunlit half are visible from Earth

questions.questionText: What is the region beyond Neptune containing many icy bodies, including Pluto, called?
questions.explanation: The Kuiper Belt is a region beyond Neptune containing many icy objects, including Pluto.

questions.questionText: The Sun is a planet.
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star, not a planet.

questions.questionText: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
questions.explanation: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to travel the average distance to Earth.

questions.questionText: There is no gravity anywhere in space.
questions.explanation: Gravity exists throughout space and keeps planets, stars, and galaxies together.

questions.questionText: Mercury is hotter on average than Venus.
questions.explanation: Venus's thick atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter on average than Mercury.

questions.questionText: The Moon produces its own light.
questions.explanation: The Moon reflects sunlight; it does not produce its own visible light.

questions.questionText: A black hole's gravity is so strong that light cannot escape from inside its Event Horizon.
All stars are the same size.
Earth takes approximately 365 days to orbit the Sun.
questions.explanation: Earth completes one orbit around the Sun in about 365.25 days, hence the additional day after every 4 years (Leap Year).

questions.questionText: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm on Saturn.
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm on Jupiter.

questions.questionText: Astronauts on the International Space Station experience microgravity, which makes them appear to float.
questions.explanation: The station and its crew are continuously falling around Earth, creating the sensation of weightlessness. It is often confused for having 'No Gravity' in space.
